title: Degreewise small products of Kan complexes are products of spaces
statement: Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, degreewise products, weak homotopy equivalences, coherent diagrams, cones and limiting cones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W})$ of $\mathcal W$-small spaces of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $J$ be a $\mathcal W$-small set, possibly empty, and let $(K_j)_{j\in J}$ be $\mathcal W$-small Kan complexes. Their degreewise product $\prod_{j\in J}K_j$ is a Kan complex, and its projections $\prod_jK_j\to K_j$, regarded as a cone in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ over the diagram $j\mapsto K_j$ indexed by the discrete simplicial set $J$, form a limiting cone. Thus $\prod_jK_j$ is a product of the $K_j$ in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$; for $J$ empty this says that $\Delta^0$ is terminal. Moreover, if $f_j:K_j\to L_j$ are weak homotopy equivalences between Kan complexes, then $\prod_jf_j$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: For every simplicial degree n, an n-simplex of the degreewise product is a tuple of n-simplices, and all face and degeneracy operators act coordinatewise. Given a horn in the product, project it to each K_j and choose a Kan filler in K_j; the tuple of fillers is a filler in the product. The empty product is the terminal simplicial set Δ^0, which is Kan. Thus the degreewise product is a Kan complex, including the empty-family case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-coherent-weight-limit-recognition] with $Y=J$ discrete, $\mathcal D=\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}$, $F(j)=K_j$ and $L=P=\prod_jK_j$. Work in an ambient universe containing this simplicial category. Here $P$ is an object of $\mathcal D$: it is a Kan complex by step 1, and it is $\mathcal W$-small because its $n$-simplices form the product $\prod_{j}(K_j)_n$ of $\mathcal W$-small sets over the $\mathcal W$-small index set $J$, and a universe is closed under such products. Its mapping simplicial sets are Kan by [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory]. The simplex-colimit rigidification of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] makes $A=\mathfrak C[J]$ discrete: every simplex of $J$ is degenerate at one vertex. The only nondegenerate simplices of $\Delta^0\star J$ are its vertices and the individual edges $b\to j$; no two nonidentity arrows compose. Thus $B(b,j)=\Delta^0$, so the weight $W_J$ is constant at $\Delta^0$ on the discrete category $A$. The projections specify $\lambda:W_J\to\mathcal D(P,F(-))$. For every Kan complex $Z$, an $n$-simplex of $\underline{\operatorname{Nat}}(W_J,\mathcal D(Z,F(-)))$ is exactly a tuple of maps $Z\times\Delta^n\to K_j$, without further naturality constraints. Such a tuple is uniquely a map $Z\times\Delta^n\to P$, and these bijections commute with every simplicial operator. Consequently postcomposition with $\lambda$ is an actual simplicial isomorphism from $\mathcal D(Z,P)$ to this enriched natural-transformation simplicial set, hence a weak homotopy equivalence. The cited recognition lemma therefore makes the projection cone limiting, in exactly the comma-cone convention of the item. No product in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ is used in this computation. If $J$ is empty, $A$ is empty, the natural-transformation simplicial set and $\operatorname{Fun}(Z,\Delta^0)$ are both $\Delta^0$; the same recognition proves terminality.

proof.text: Let $f_j:K_j\to L_j$ be the given weak homotopy equivalences. In the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core], factor $(1,f_j):K_j\to K_j\times L_j$ as a trivial cofibration $i_j:K_j\to Z_j$ followed by a Kan fibration $p_j:Z_j\to K_j\times L_j$. Set $r_j=\operatorname{pr}_1p_j$ and $q_j=\operatorname{pr}_2p_j$, so $r_ji_j=1$ and $q_ji_j=f_j$. Both $r_j,q_j$ are Kan fibrations: to lift a horn against $r_j$, first extend the missing $L_j$ coordinate using that $L_j$ is Kan, then lift the resulting horn square against $p_j$; for $q_j$ extend the $K_j$ coordinate instead. Since $i_j$ and $f_j$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three in this model structure gives that $r_j$ and $q_j$ are weak equivalences. Thus both are trivial fibrations. This construction uses the Kan hypotheses on BOTH $K_j$ and $L_j$ and does not assert that $f_j$ itself is a fibration.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-model-product-weak-equivalence] to the two families of trivial fibrations $r_j:Z_j\to K_j$ and $q_j:Z_j\to L_j$ constructed in step 3. All degreewise products exist, so $R=\prod_jr_j$ and $Q=\prod_jq_j$ are weak equivalences. Put $I=\prod_ji_j$. Coordinatewise composition gives $RI=1$ and $QI=\prod_jf_j$. Two-out-of-three for the model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] first makes $I$ a weak equivalence from $RI=1$ and $R$, and then makes $QI$ a weak equivalence from $Q$ and $I$. This proves the final clause. For $J=\varnothing$, every product map here is the identity of $\Delta^0$.
